Encode and decode bytes

Source: R/encode.R
id_encode.Rd

id_encode() writes bytes of any length as text in a form, and id_decode() reads them back. A UUID's text forms are the 16-byte case: id_format(x, form) is id_encode(id_bytes(x), form).

Usage

id_encode(bytes, form, alphabet = NULL, sep = "-")

id_decode(text, form, alphabet = NULL, width = NULL)

Arguments

bytes

A raw vector (one element), a list of raw vectors (NULL for a missing element), or a raw matrix with one element per column. At most 65536 bytes per element.

form

The form.

alphabet

For form = "alphabet", its symbols in digit order: 2 to 94 distinct printable ASCII characters other than space. NULL for ShortUUID's.

sep

The separator between units for "proquint" and "words". It must not contain letters.

text

A character vector.

width

NULL, or the number of bytes each element must decode to.

Value

id_encode(): a character vector, NA where bytes is NULL. id_decode(): a list of raw vectors, with NULL where text is NA or not text of the form.

Details

Each form writes what the mainstream Go and Python libraries write, so text made elsewhere decodes here and the other way round:

  • "hex": lowercase hexadecimal. Decoding takes either case and ignores hyphens.

  • "base32": Crockford's alphabet, with the spare bits in front as zero bits, as ULID and TypeID do. Sixteen bytes give 26 characters starting 0 to 7, so a UUID in this form is textually a ULID. Uppercase, and either case on input; the letters I, L, O and U are rejected.

  • "base32rfc", "base32hex": RFC 4648 sections 6 and 7, with the spare bits at the end and no padding. Decoding also takes = padding.

  • "base36": 0-9a-z, fixed width; 16 bytes are Uuid25's 25 characters.

  • "base58": base58btc. Each leading zero byte is one 1, so the length varies, as in Bitcoin and Go's and Python's base58.

  • "base62", "base62sort": 0-9A-Za-z, fixed width, padded with 0; sorts as the bytes do. The two names are one form.

  • "base64url": RFC 4648 section 5, no padding. Decoding also takes = padding.

  • "base64sort": base64url's bits in the IETF draft's alphabet, in ASCII order, so it sorts as the bytes do.

  • "alphabet": the caller's symbols, most significant digit first, fixed width, padded with the first symbol. The default is ShortUUID's 57 symbols, as ShortUUID 1.0 and later write them.

  • "proquint": each 16 bits as five pronounceable letters.

  • "words": each 16 bits as a Niceware word. The Niceware list was not checked for offensive words, and some text in this form may offend.

The fixed-width forms ("base32", "base36", "base62", "alphabet") write the digits the byte count needs, so the length gives the byte count back. "proquint" and "words" take an even number of bytes, and their decoding ignores case and any non-letter between units.

Examples

b <- as.raw(c(0xf8, 0x1d, 0x4f, 0xae))
id_encode(b, "base58")
#> [1] "7LqmvD"
id_decode("7R3N7TW", "base32")
#> [[1]]
#> NULL
#> 
x <- id_parse("f81d4fae-7dec-11d0-a765-00a0c91e6bf6", "uuid")
id_encode(id_bytes(x), "base62")
#> [1] "7YBUWgZR1mKSqGyj9tVViw"
id_format(x, "proquint")
#> [1] "zobit-huvov-lulos-dalib-pitoj-bafob-sohiv-kozuk"
id_encode(id_bytes(x), "alphabet", alphabet = "0123456789")
#> [1] "329800735698586629295641978511506172918"
